notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 23% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is day to day and has missed the last 15 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Michael Carcone is out 3-4 months (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward.
They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 3 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Dawson Mercer takes shifts on two lines, L3 and L4.

Dylan DeMelo is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Josh Morrissey has taken his spot beside Mario Ferraro. That pair has had 47% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:30 together, about what it had with DeMelo (51%).
Isak Rosén is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. Viggo Björck has taken his spot beside Adam Lowry and Alex Iafallo.
Henry Thrun was added to the roster on Nov 14 and has played beside Mario Ferraro.
Danil Zhilkin was added to the roster on Nov 18 and has played beside Alex Iafallo and Cole Koepke.
Jack St. Ivany is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 4 games, down from 35% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Jets go in seventh in the Central with 26 points, a point behind the Mammoth, sixth. A regulation win for the Jets would lift them past the Mammoth.

WPG.head: The Jets face a real test
WPG.body: Even though Winnipeg has home-ice advantage and Utah will be without Schmidt, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Jets can pull it off if their power play gets going.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a lot going for them

story.head: Who drives the play: the Mammoth
paras: The Jets (11-9-4) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Vegas on Saturday, while the Mammoth have won two in a row. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth sixth (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Jets seventh (18th). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.562) says: their chances are worth about .699, and their goaltending has held them back. The Jets’ record (.542) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), let the point shots come and guard the net (1st) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (3rd). On the other side, the Jets get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd) and rarely ice the puck (4th). They also create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd), and that sets up a fight with the Mammoth’s power play (9th), which could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (28th). The Mammoth shoot a lot, but the Jets don’t.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 23 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, and Logan Cooley (12 G / 13 A / 25 P in 21 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. Kyle Connor (19 G / 11 A / 30 P in 24 GP) is tied for the Jets’ scoring lead, with nine points in his last five games. Mark Scheifele (8 G / 22 A / 30 P in 24 GP) shares it, with eleven points in his last five games.
Sebastian Cossa (6-2-1 / .887 SV% in 9 GS) is expected to start for Utah, and Stuart Skinner (7-5-4 / .883 SV% in 17 GS) for Winnipeg.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.

items.text: Clayton Keller has missed the Mammoth’s latest game.

The Mammoth are newly without Michael Carcone, and have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino and Nick Schmaltz for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Jets have been without Dylan DeMelo and Isak Rosén for several games.
Gabriel Vilardi has three goals on chances worth about 8.3 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
